contents.name: §5.3, affine schemes, open subschemes, and affine opens
§5.3.2, Definitions: open subschemes and affine open subsets
§5.5.5, Projective and quasiprojective schemes
contents.reason: The projective and quasiprojective programme needs graded-ring and Proj machinery beyond the selected general-scheme interface; the one P^1 gluing computation is retained only as a concrete test of the gluing theorem.

contents.name: §6.3.3, affine-local properties including Noetherian and finite type
§6.4, Normality and factoriality
contents.reason: Normality, factoriality, and their local algebra require a distinct divisor and singularity development; neither property is used to define finite-type morphisms or the closed-subscheme constructions here.

contents.name: §6.5, Associated points and primary ideals
contents.reason: Associated primes and primary decomposition are later Noetherian-module tools, not logical prerequisites of the page's affine-local definitions, reduction, or scheme-theoretic-image construction.

contents.name: §7.2, Morphisms of ringed spaces and affine morphisms
§7.3, Morphisms of schemes and schemes over a base
§7.3.F, maps to Spec A and global sections
§7.4, morphisms of Proj schemes and Veronese subrings
contents.reason: The general Proj-morphism and Veronese theory relies on the graded projective construction rather than the affine-local morphism technology that this page establishes; it is deferred to projective geometry.

sources.title: The Stacks Project, Schemes
sources.locator: Contents, PDF viewer page 0; §§7–14, viewer pages 11–26, and §§19–24, viewer pages 35–48. Read the named sections `Quasi-coherent sheaves on affines`, `Closed subspaces of affine schemes`, `Schemes`, `Immersions of schemes`, `Zariski topology of schemes`, `Reduced schemes`, `Points of schemes`, `Glueing schemes`, `Quasi-compact morphisms`, `Universal closedness`, `Separation axioms`, `Valuative criterion of separation`, `Monomorphisms`, and `Functoriality of quasi-coherent modules`; in §21 read Definition 21.3 and Lemma 21.7 (tag 01KP) in full.

contents.name: §8, Lemma 8.2: closed subspaces of an affine scheme
§20, Universal closedness
contents.reason: Universal closedness is a properness precursor involving arbitrary base change and closed maps; it is neither implied by nor needed for the finite-type and subscheme results selected for this page.

contents.name: §21, Separation axioms; Definition 21.3 and Lemma 21.7 (affine-open criterion; tag 01KP)
§22, Valuative criterion of separation
contents.reason: The valuative uniqueness criterion requires the diagonal definition of separatedness plus valuation-ring interfaces and is explicitly part of the later AV-14 pair, rather than a result needed to construct schemes or closed subschemes.

contents.name: §23, Monomorphisms
contents.reason: The section's diagonal characterisation and closure properties belong with the later AV-14 treatment after fibre products; they are not used by the affine-overlap condition retained here.

contents.name: §24, Functoriality of quasi-coherent modules
contents.reason: Pushforward and functoriality of quasi-coherent modules require the later sheaf/coherent-module programme; this page uses only the affine-local quasi-coherent ideal interface needed for closed subschemes.

contents.name: §6, Lemma 6.7: image from a reduced source

contents.name: §22, Lemmas 22.3–22.7
